entry.title: Days 66 and 67: Bus from Vlorë to Himarë, then Bike to Sarandë

link.title: Days 66 and 67: Bus from Vlorë to Himarë, then Bike to Sarandë

entry.content:
My last night in Vlorë was terrible. There was one guest, an older fat lady, who complained that she felt cold when the AC was on. It was 30C, or 86F, inside the dorm. I don’t understand how she could be feeling cold when it’s so hot. Of course, Nana sided with her since she has an excuse to not turn on the AC in the room. I slept through the heat and I was not happy.

The next morning, I rode my bike to the bus station hoping to get on the bus to Himarë. When I got there, the driver first wanted 4000 Lek, which is €40, for me and my bicycle. I was told by a fellow the day before that it was only going to be 700 Lek, so needless to say I was shocked by the price. Then the driver reduced the price to 3000 Lek, saying 1000 Lek for me and 2000 Lek for my bicycle. I knew I was getting scammed.

I asked other drivers regarding the fare, they all told me 3000 Lek to Himarë. I realized it’s now too late to start cycling to Himarë and there’s a massive hill that I have to cycle over, not to mention the distance. I decided to get scammed so I didn’t have to cycle.

This was the first time that I got scammed in Albania. I guess not all Albanians are good people. Actually, not all people are good people. There will be some bad apples.

After two hours on the bus, I arrived in Himarë. The place that I booked in Himarë is a camping site since all other options were not available on booking.com, unless I wanted to pay more for a hotel. The camping site is called Camping Himara and it’s not too far from Livadi Beach. I had to cycle about 2 miles to get there from the bus stop in Himarë.

The camping site has a bar area. I actually liked the place since it’s on a hill and has a great view.

I went down to the beach only to see that it’s not a sandy beach, but full of little rocks and pebbles. Plus, there were so many umbrellas and glamping tents that I felt a very touristy vibe. Since I’m traveling solo, I didn’t feel like renting an umbrella and chill on the beach by myself. I only stayed for about ten minutes before walking back to the campsite.

If I had known that I didn’t really like the beach I would have stayed on the bus all the way to Sarandë. No use to worry about past mistakes.

I spent the rest of the day chatting with some guests who were also staying at the campground. I also noticed my back tire was leaking air at the base of the valve. I fixed that. I also adjusted the tension on the carbon belt since it needed tightening.

I thought hard about whether to ride my bike to Sarandë the next day or get scammed again and take the bus there. I decided to ride my bike even though I have to ride 36 miles and go over two mountain passes.

Yesterday morning, I started my ride at sunrise. The first major hill was at 12 miles mark. I had to push my bike at certain points because I just didn’t have the energy to ride up the hill. By the time I reached the other side I drank all my water. Luckily, there was a small market and I bought some water for the next big hill. Usually, I don’t need a refill at all when I ride, but this day was different because of the hills.

The scenery was fantastic when I was up in the mountains. I could see a town underneath me and the sea. The Albanian riviera is fantastic!

As I came to another market, I decided to refill my water bottles again and eat a byrek, which is a Balkan pastry with stuffing inside. I chose the meat stuffing because I needed the protein. The other options were spinach or cheese.

The downhills were the dangerous part where I had to be very careful. I was squeezing my brake levers most of the time as there were hairpin turns. For the last 15 miles or so to Sarandë, the road was either slightly downhill or flat. With the mountains to my left side, I had a blissful time coming to the city limit of Sarandë.

In Sarandë, the traffic was bad since it was around 10:30 AM when I arrived. The cops were directing traffic badly as if they didn’t know anything about traffic patterns. Finally, after 36 miles, two large hills, and 4:45 hours of riding, I reached Mega Hostel, the place where I’ll be spending four nights.

I was so sweaty and tired that I didn’t do anything except eating lunch and dinner at nearby restaurants, then taking a shower at the hostel. I ended up going to sleep at around 7 PM.

This morning, since the temperature was cooler, I took a stroll to Sarandë Promenade. The beach there is also a pebble beach, which I didn’t like. At the ferry booth, I bought a ticket to Corfu, Greece, for €37, on Thursday morning at 10 AM. This price includes the €5 bicycle fare.

I don’t know what else to do in Sarandë. It’s the last Albanian town that I’m stay at. There are boat tour to other points of interest if I choose to do that. To be honest, I just want to relax and not do too much.

entry.title: Days 64 and 65: Levan to Vlorë, then a Rest Day in Vlorë

link.title: Days 64 and 65: Levan to Vlorë, then a Rest Day in Vlorë

entry.content:
My last night in Levan was terrible. There was no AC so it was very hot in the room with only one small fan. Someone rang the doorbell at midnight for some reason. And there was firework at 1 AM. I don’t know what they were celebrating, but at least it was short lived.

Soon after I started my ride the next morning, it started to rain. My weather app didn’t even forecast rain. I pulled aside to a cafe and had a cup of Albanian coffee, which is served in a shot glass, similar to an espresso.

A local Albanian guy and I started chatting. He was very kind, like many Albanian people. We didn’t talk too much, but he was impressed by my bike tour. In the end, he ended up paying for my coffee. What a generous guy!

I only had to ride 16 miles to Vlorë from Levan and I was glad for that. As I got closer to town, the view was magnificent when I cruised down the hill. There are mountains on the sides and the town is tucked right in the valley where the Ionian Sea and the Adriatic Sea meet. Unfortunately, I didn’t take any photos since I was going downhill so fast.

I arrived at Nana Hostel at 7:30 AM. My clothes were damp from the rain. The owner of the hostel, who is an old lady named Nana, did my laundry. She was so bossy to the other guests and refused to keep the AC on for long so she can save money. She also didn’t provide shampoo to any guests. Not that I needed any. I found her to be the highlight of my stay in Vlorë.

I didn’t do much yesterday afternoon and only rode my bike to get dinner at an Asian restaurant called Nishiki. It’s a mom-and-pop restaurant and the food was so good.

This morning, I rode my bike to the bus station to ask about a bus to Himarë since I don’t want to ride my bike up a giant hill from Vlorë to Himarë tomorrow. The guy assured me that there’s a bus at 7 AM that can take my bike. I hope he’s right.

I did all my Vlorë sightseeing in the morning. There isn’t too much to see. I saw the Independence Monument then rode my bike to Lungomare Beach. The temperature gets hotter later in the day so I came back to the hostel around 10:30.

I spent rest of the morning and most of the afternoon coding a website that will combine my web development portfolio with my photography portfolio and adding a blogging feature. When I’m done bike touring Europe, I will start blogging my next adventure using that website since it doesn’t rely on Google services and might work in China if I decide to go there.

Right now, I feel I’m done cycling. I might even take the bus from Himarë to Sarandë, then take the ferry to Corfu, Greece. It’s just too hot and I only ride about 30 miles max per day. I just want to go back home and get some things done on my to-do list. And for some weird reason, I have a feeling that I might get stopped by ICE at the Philadelphia Airport and be detained and deported. My mind thinks too much sometimes.

entry.title: Days 62 and 63: Durrës to Divjakë, then to Levan

link.title: Days 62 and 63: Durrës to Divjakë, then to Levan

entry.content:
Yesterday morning, I woke up at 5:10 and got on the road at the time of the sunrise, 5:35 AM.

I was glad to be out of the Backpackers Hostel in Durrës because the place was messy and had no AC. I also didn’t have a good vibe there. It was a complete switch from the Mosaic Home hostel in Tiranë, where it was one of the best hostels I’ve stayed at.

In any case, I rode on a service road next to the main highway most of the way. The route followed the EuroVelo the entire time. I reached Olive Guesthouse (Fori Vodo) in Divjakë around 9 AM after riding 35 miles. The owners are an old couple. They were very nice and offered me coffee and some watermelon slices. I stayed in a private room and it had AC. What a wonderful delight!

I didn’t do much in Divjakë because it’s a small town. Except for going out for lunch and dinner I mainly rested in the room and took a nap.

Google somehow flagged my website as “malicious” so it was down for a day. That was a good excuse for me to not write a blog post yesterday. After I disputed it, this website is up again.

This made me think if I care enough about blogging my travels. I mainly do it to remember my adventures. Maybe I should consider moving my blog to WordPress or something other than Blogger if Google gives me any more issues.

This morning, I continued my bicycle journey by following the EuroVelo. I saw some half finished houses on the sides of the road. There were some goats and geese, too. It felt like I went back in time, seeing old bicycles and old cars on the road.

This is the typical Albania I’ve been witnessing the entire time while traveling in this country. Not to say there aren’t any rich people in the country, I did see a new Bentley in Tiranë and some modern BMWs. But the majority of the people own 20+ years old cars or ride on old bicycles that look like they are about to fall apart. My bike must look like a Cadillac to them.

To me, it’s not the material wealth that matters anyway. The Albanian people I’ve met have been very kind and generous. They are the type of people I would like to live with.

After riding 28 miles to Levan, I arrived at Kappa Guesthouse. The lady just finished cleaning and I was able to check-in right away.

Levan is even smaller than Divjakë with only a few stores and restaurants. The owner of the guesthouse had to work at the restaurant where I had my lunch.

My room doesn’t have AC, only a fan. The temperature in the afternoon is now 35C, or 95F. I plan on going out one more time to get dinner. Tomorrow I’ll ride to Vlorë and stay there for two nights since it’s a bigger town.

entry.title: Days 59 to 61: Tiranë to Durrës, then Two Days in Durrës

link.title: Days 59 to 61: Tiranë to Durrës, then Two Days in Durrës

entry.content:
Before I left Tiranë, I met another long distance cyclist at the hostel. His name is Johannes and he’s from Germany. We had dinner together and it was nice talking to another cyclist. Johannes started from Germany and is making a loop around the Balkans before going back home to start his job in September.

The next morning, I started my ride to Durrës at 5:30. I mainly cycled along a service road that ran parallel to the main road. When I reached the Backpackers Hostel in Durrës I had ridden about 26 miles.

There isn’t much to do in Durrës. In the afternoon, I walked to The Venetian Tower of Durrës, Durrës Amphitheater, and the Byzantine Forum. None of them impressed me. Once I went to Rome, no ruins are worth seeing.

In the hostel, I met a Chinese guy named Qu. We hung out the next day and walked to Durrës Beach. Surprisingly, it’s the only Balkan beach that I’ve been to that has sand. But the temperature was so hot that we only stayed for about an hour before taking a taxi back to the hostel.

There’s another Chinese woman who arrived at the hostel yesterday. Her English name is Teresa. The three of us might grab dinner together tonight. I plan on leaving at 5:30 tomorrow morning to cycle to Divjakë so I have to sleep early tonight.

entry.title: Days 54 to 58: Five Days in Tiranë

link.title: Days 54 to 58: Five Days in Tiranë

entry.content:
I spent five days in Tiranë, the capital of Albania. The first couple of days I hung out with a Dutch girl named Lotte and a Turkish guy named Ismail from the hostel.

We had lunch together and walked to the square in the middle of the city. We also went to Bunk’Art 2, which I thought would be an art gallery of some sort, but it’s about the history of Albania during WWII. There is also the Pyramid of Tirana that I climbed to the top to see some views.

A couple of days later, I rode my bicycle to Dajti Ekspres station and took the cable car to the top of Dajti Mountain. It had great views of the city, but not much to do there.

The past couple of days were very hot. I basically chilled at the hostel and chatted with two Chinese travelers. One is a 21 years old film student who doesn’t have an English name so I’ll call him Gao. The other traveler is in his early 30s and has been traveling on and off for ten years. His English name is Ruke. I haven’t spoken that much Chinese in a long time. It was good to talk to them.

Albania is one of the cheaper countries to stay at. The hostel is only €11 per night. I guess I picked a good country to stay for a month.

Tomorrow, I’ll cycle to Durrës. It’ll be about 26 miles and I hope to get there early in the day.

entry.title: Day 53: Lezhë to Tiranë
entry.content:
This morning, I left Vila Kastriotet-Hotel at 5:30 and rode about 43 miles to Tiranë. It took me about four and half hours with a rest stop for a soft drink at a gas station.

I was finally honked at by an Albanian driver when I was trying to navigate a roundabout. I guess I was just supposed to cut in rather than wait for the cars to go pass. In any case, the drivers in Eastern Europe have been very patient with me and this was certainly an exception.

I arrived at the Mosaic Home hostel in Tiranë a little before 10 AM and waited until 1 PM to check in. After settling down and taking a shower, I went on the hunt for some ramen since I haven’t had any Asian food in a while.

The first ramen restaurant I went to was 30 minutes away by walking. I was disappointed to find out that the ramen restaurant only offered instant ramen that the customer had to cook. It reminded me of the Seinfeld episode when Kramer tried to sell his make-your-own-pizza idea. I didn’t want to eat instant ramen so I only bought a boba tea there.

I walked along the lake in the Tirana Lake Park before finding another noodle shop called Kungfu Noodle Bar. This time, I had some delicious noodles.

I’m back at the hostel now. Realistically, I think Tiranë is only worth two or three days of exploration. Since I have plenty of time before getting to Greece on August 13 I plan on staying in Tiranë for about 5 or 6 days before moving on to Durrës.

entry.title: Day 52: Shkodër to Lezhë
entry.content:
Yesterday afternoon, I had the honor of putting my handprints on the wall at Chuck and Susan’s place. I made my handprints look like little feet as that’s something I didn’t see anyone do. What can I say, I like to be different.

I fell asleep early and didn’t get a chance to properly say goodbye to Chuck and Susan. But I’m so glad that I was hosted by them. They are legends in the Warmshowers community and it’s definitely one of the highlights of my trip.

This morning, I left their apartment at 5:30 to start my ride to Lezhë. The route on Organic Maps took me on the major road, SH1, for most of the time. The morning traffic was light. Then I turned to a gravel path with tall plants on both sides of me. I didn’t like it so much since it felt like I was riding in a jungle. When I reached a more rural road I was glad there was pavement and fewer cars. Eventually, I returned to SH1 and rode into Lezhë. I arrived at Vila Kastriotet-Hotel around 8 AM after riding 26.7 miles.

After checking in at 10 AM, I took a shower then walked around the town. There were only a few things to see, the Skanderbeg Tomb and Lezhë Castle. I opted not to hike up the hill to Lezhë Castle and only walked around the site of the Skanderbeg Tomb. I didn’t think much of it and didn’t pay the 200 LEK to go inside.

Back in the hotel room, I learned that Heinz Stücke passed away three days ago on July 22. He’s the cyclist who bicycled around the world continuously for over 50 years. I met him last year and admired him greatly because he lived a life that he chose, not based on what society determined. He’s a legend who influenced many cyclists. May he rest in peace.

I’ve had a lot of time to think and reflect on my life and life in general. I feel very happy and content right now. I have everything I need. When I get back home I will downsize more. Life on a bicycle made me appreciate all the things I carry. My mind is satisfied and I’m physically healthy. What more can I ask. I also have to remind myself that nothing is as good as it is and nothing is as bad as it is. Follow the Middle Way. And be grateful for what I have and what I’m experiencing.

entry.title: Days 46 to 51: Six More Days in Shkodër

link.title: Days 46 to 51: Six More Days in Shkodër

entry.content:
I stayed at Chuck and Susan’s apartment for another six days, making a total of nine days. Chuck told me that I’m now tied for the longest stays at their place. I’m very grateful that they allowed to me stay this long. Previously, I thought about getting a hostel, but Chuck extended his invitation.

I did some chores around the apartment, including sweeping the patio, taking down two doors, and sharpening some knives. I also cleaned my bicycle and donated a few things from my panniers for future cyclists.

Shkodër reminds me of Asia with all the bicycles. Albania is still a developing country with the occasional water outages that happened in the past few days as they are still trying to complete the city’s infrastructure.

Overall, I had a great time in Shkodër. It was definitely a change of pace going from cycling to a more slow-down life. Tomorrow, I’ll resume cycling and ride 26 miles south to Lezhë.

entry.title: Days 42 to 45: Two Rest Days in Shkodër and a Hike from Valbonë to Theth

link.title: Days 42 to 45: Two Rest Days in Shkodër and a Hike from Valbonë to Theth

entry.content:
As it turned out, only one cyclist showed up a few days ago. Her name is Niamh and she’s from the United Kingdom. Her front tire got a puncture while coming here so she spent some time finding a new tire in town. The following day, we cycled to the nearby lake town of Shiroka and chilled on the bank for a bit before cycling back.

Niamh told me about the hike she did the last time she was in Albania. It was organized by her hostel, The Wanderers Hostel. The hike is six hours long from Valbonë to Theth. There’s also a separate hike to a waterfall and a pool called the Blue Eye in Theth. I decided to sign up with the hostel. So for the past two nights I was in the Albanian Alps.

The trip to Valbonë took about seven hours from Shkodër. It consisted of a bus ride to Koman, a ferry to Fierzë, then a minibus ride to the Adenisi Guest House.

Since the trip was organized by the hostel, everybody knew each other beforehand except me. I tried to be social, but still felt ostracized since everyone was in their early twenties and most of them were paired already, either as couples or as friends.

In any case, I took a nap at the hostel and didn’t even eat lunch. The dinner provided by the guest house was too shy on the meats and I only had one chicken leg as the protein. However, I did pack three boiled eggs, along with a few other things, for the hike the next morning.

The hostel manager drove us to the trailhead and we started hiking around 6:30 AM. It took me two hours to hike to the top of the mountain then about 3.5 hours down to Guesthouse Dreni in Theth. The view was great, but on the way down I slipped several time since I didn’t hike with hiking shoes, just regular walking shoes. There were some cafes along the hiking route but I kept going.

I was one of the first few hikers from the group to reach the hostel in Theth. Apparently, I would have been the first one if the people before me didn’t catch a ride.

This guesthouse had a buffet style dinner and I ate a full meal by the time I went to bed. I slept for almost 12 hours last night.

This morning, I opted not to do the hike to the waterfall and Blue Eye because yesterday’s hike was the longest hike I’ve ever done in my life. I simply didn’t want to hike anymore, so I took the minibus back to Shkodër.

When I arrived back at Chuck and Susan’s place I met a German couple and a French couple. I didn’t quite catch any of their names since they are all busy doing something.

I really don’t know what to do for the next several days. According to my current plan, I  will stay in Shkodër for six more nights before cycling farther south.

entry.title: Days 40 and 41: Budva to Bar, then to Shkodër, Albania

link.title: Days 40 and 41: Budva to Bar, then to Shkodër, Albania

entry.content:
Yesterday, I started my ride from Budva at the usual time of 5:30 AM. I cycled on the main road most of the time and the occasional side roads. At one point, I had to push my bike up a steep hill with switchbacks. The hill was so steep that I had to stop and rest on every turn so my calves can get a break. Even though the journey was only 23.5 miles to Bar, it took me three hours to get to Sova Smart House hostel.

I was able to self check-in, but I still had to wait for the hostel manager to show up so I can pay. As I was waiting, another guest showed up. Her name is Kristen and she’s a 36 years old makeup artist from California. We hit it off right away.

Kristen loves hiking and just spent ten days hiking the Peaks of Balkans trail that connects Albania, Kosovo, and Montenegro. She is also financially independent, but doesn’t realize it yet. We ended up spending the rest of the day together going to the beachside, visiting the Church of St. John Vladimir, and eating lunch.

Talking to her is like talking to a female version of myself. We both feel traveling is our main goal in life and being independent is very important for both of us. Of all the people I met during my travels we have the most in common. I had a blast hanging out with her for a day.

This morning, I started my ride at 5:20 and rode up one more big but gradual hill before coming into Albania. The border crossing was much better this time when the agent waved me to the front of a line of cars so I got processed faster.

I arrived in the city of Shkodër at 9 AM after 32 miles of riding. I’ll be staying at the most famous Warmshowers hosts’ place for tonight. They are an American couple who chose to retire in Albania. They are Chuck and Susan.

Upon entering their apartment, I saw the famous wall of palm prints of all the cyclists who had stayed here. Then I was greeted by Susan, Chuck’s wife. Over a glass of iced water, Chuck and I chatted about what to expect while stay at their place. I learned that him and Susan have hosted almost 1600 cyclists in the past seven years. That’s just amazing!

For lunch, I ate at Chuck and Susan’s favorite restaurant, Puri. I ordered the Father’s Rice meal and it was THE meal for a long distance cyclist, with rice, meat, beans, and salad.

I’m now back at Chuck and Susan’s apartment. There will be three more cyclists coming in today. It’ll be a very lively group of people here for the night.

I plan to stay in Albania for a month, but I don’t know how many days I want to stay in Shkodër and where. I’ll decide on that soon.

entry.summary: Yesterday, I started my ride from Budva at the usual time of 5:30 AM. I cycled on the main road most of the time and the occasional side roads. At one point, I had to push my bike up a steep hill with switchbacks. The hill was so steep that I had to stop and rest on every turn so my calves can get a break. Even though the journey was only 23.5 miles to Bar, it took me three hours to get to Sova Smart House hostel.
